name: Zichri
overview: Zichri is a male figure from the tribe of Benjamin, known primarily as the father of Joel. His mention is brief and specific, with no additional notes or detailed narrative about his life or character. He appears in Scripture as a genealogical reference within the post-exilic community.
namesAndTitles: The name Zichri means 'y-h-v-h remembers,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning tied to God's faithfulness. It is a proper name recorded in Nehemiah 11:9 and is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Zichri as the father of Joel, establishing a direct paternal relationship. He is explicitly identified as a descendant of the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Zichri's significance lies in his role within the genealogical records of the returned exiles, highlighting the continuity of the Benjaminite lineage after the Babylonian captivity. His mention as Joel's father situates him within the restored community in Jerusalem, underscoring the importance of family heritage in God's ongoing covenant people. Though not a prominent narrative character, Zichri contributes to the biblical record of God's faithfulness in preserving His people.
